A cloud SLA is a promise (we'll be up X% of the time) plus a penalty (a service credit if we miss).

99.9% uptime allows about 8.77 hours of downtime a year and still counts as kept. The credit refunds a slice of your bill, not your lost sales. And the SLA covers the provider's infrastructure, not your single server or your bad deploy.

thread:
Cloud SLA, Decoded: What "99.9% Uptime" Actually Buys You

Quick thread 🧵
A cloud SLA is a promise (we'll be up X% of the time) plus a penalty (a service credit if we miss).
99.9% uptime allows about 8.77 hours of downtime a year and still counts as kept.
The credit refunds a slice of your bill, not your lost sales.
And the SLA covers the provider's infrastructure, not your single server or your bad deploy.
